question:
Context Question: Henrik Ibsen - A Doll's House
'The very fact of your pleading his cause makes it impossible for me to keep him. Everyone at the bank already knows that I intend to dismiss him. If the rumour got about that the new manager had allowed his wife to persuade him to change his mind (Act 2, P.534).'
(i) Who is the speaker?
(ii) Whom is he addressing?
(iii) Identify the location where this speech is made.
(iv) Who is the subject of this discourse?
(v) What is the speaker trying to protect?
modelAnswer: Model answer required. (i. Torvald Helmer, ii. Nora Helmer, iii. The Helmer's home/study, iv. Nils Krogstad, v. His reputation and authority as the new bank manager).

question:

(i) Who's the speaker?
(ii) Who is the speaker addressing?
(iii) What matter is addressed here?

modelAnswer: Model answer required. (i. Nils Krogstad, ii. Nora Helmer, iii. The forged signature on the loan, iv. The crime of forgery which could ruin Torvald's career, v. Kept secret, concealed).

subject: Literature
question:
Context Question: William Shakespeare - Othello
'O heaven! How got she out? O treason of the blood!
Fathers, from hence trust not daughter's minds
By what you see them act. Is there not charms
By which property of youth and maidhood
May be abused? Have you not read of some such thing? (Act 1 Scene 1)'
(i) Who is the speaker?
(ii) Who is being addressed?
(iii) Who is the speaker discussing?
(iv) What is the meaning of the expression: 'From hence trust not daughter's minds'
(v) 'By what you see them act' conveys what negative attitude?
modelAnswer: Model answer required. (i. Brabantio, ii. Othello (and the Duke/Senators), iii. Desdemona, iv. Fathers should not trust their daughters based on their outward behavior, v. That women are deceptive and their actions are merely performances to hide their true nature).

subject: Literature
question:
Context Question: William Shakespeare - Othello
'Keep up your bright swords, for the dew will rust them.
Good signor, you shall more command with years
Than with your weapons (Act 1, Scene 2)'
(i) Who is speaking?
(ii) To whom?
(iii) Describe the atmosphere here
(iv) Explain the meaning of the last line
modelAnswer: Model answer required. (i. Othello, ii. Brabantio and his armed men, iii. Tense and violent, but quickly calmed by Othello's authority, iv. Othello is stating that Brabantio's age should command more respect than his weapons; he should use his wisdom rather than violence).
